source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (official EU procurement portal, search UI)
why_relevant: Single mandatory publication venue for all Czech above-threshold contract notices, award notices and modifications. Contains CZ banking/payment-services tenders (CPV 66xxxxx, 72xxxxxx for card/ATM systems) in structured, multilingual form, with buyer name, NUTS CZ region, value, procedure type and — in award notices — the winning supplier. This is the core A2 spine for the CZ cell.

Working groups (eGovernment, kybernetická bezpečnost, veřejné zakázky) reveal which vendors organise around which state procurement themes — a cheap proxy for which suppliers are positioning for upcoming public IT/payment tenders.

source_name: Svaz průmyslu a dopravy ČR (SP ČR) – member entry for Česká fintech asociace / odvětvové svazy
why_relevant: SP ČR republishes affiliated sector associations' profiles including enumerated member companies — this page carried an explicit fintech member roster (AKCENTA, BONDSTER, ComGate, GOPAY, MONET+, Twisto, Zentity …). Acts as a second, independently-maintained copy of association rosters and a hub to other 'odvětvové svazy'.

source_name: ARES / obchodní rejstřík — Czech registrations of group procurement and shared-service entities
why_relevant: Erste Group Procurement states it has its own subsidiary in the Czech Republic, and Erste Digital has a Prague site. Resolving those legal entities (name, IČO, registered office, statutory bodies, filed financial statements in the Sbírka listin) converts a vague 'group sourcing arm' into a named contracting party you can then trace through the contract register, court filings and job ads. Note: I did not confirm the specific Erste Group Procurement CZ entity name/IČO in this run.

~101 senior IT executives (including from banks) as individual members. Its member roster appears not to be published, so value is in event programmes and the CACIO fórum agendas, which name the organisations and decision-makers steering IT investment — an actor-map source rather than a directory.

entity_name: Commercial TED mirrors / tender alert services
source_name: Commercial TED mirrors / tender alert services (TenderWolf, Tenderlake, Tendersontime, jorpex, tedapi.pro)
why_relevant: Commercial resellers of TED content. Low evidentiary value (derivative, paywalled, unclear freshness) but useful in two ways: their public notice pages are sometimes indexed by search engines when the TED page is not, and their knowledge-base articles explain publication mechanics clearly. Treat as lead-generation, never as citation of record.

High-volume regional/national daily; freely republishes and summarises procurement-scandal reporting originated by paywalled outlets, and covers municipal/regional tenders (transport, ticketing, municipal payment services) that national media skip.

source_name: Dopravní podnik města Brna (DPMB) – news on card payment / e-ticketing rollout
why_relevant: Operator announcements date and describe validator/EMV rollouts (cited cost ~65m CZK), giving the context and timing needed to locate the underlying tender on the Brno buyer profile and to anticipate replacement cycles.

source_name: dZakazky.cz – supplier-side tender search and e-mail watchdog
why_relevant: Supplier-facing aggregator of above- and below-threshold municipal and other public tenders with a trial e-mail watchdog; another commercial mirror useful for cross-checking coverage gaps of the big platforms.

source_name: Finance.cz – mirror listing of ČLFA members (seznamy a adresáře)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator mirror of the ČLFA roster; useful as a redundancy/cross-check source when the association site is restructured, and it sits inside a broader 'seznamy a adresáře' directory hub that points at further financial-sector lists.
Aggregates English-language bank vacancies in Prague, useful as a cross-check for roles not posted in Czech; also surfaces vendor/consultancy roles staffed against bank programmes.

entity_name: International commercial tender aggregators covering CZ
source_name: International commercial tender aggregators covering CZ (Tendersinfo, BidDetail, TenderImpulse, Jorpex)
why_relevant: Paid English-language mirrors of CZ tenders. Low unique value (they re-publish VVZ/TED) but useful as an English-language cross-check and for cross-border comparison; Jorpex publishes a country guide naming the underlying CZ sources.

entity_name: Municipal 'Registr smluv' pages on public-body websites
source_name: Municipal 'Registr smluv' pages on public-body websites (e.g. Praha-Dolni Mecholupy)
why_relevant: Many municipalities and districts maintain their own contract listing alongside the central register, sometimes with contracts below the CZK 50k threshold or with less redaction. Useful for filling gaps at the small-buyer end, where banking and terminal contracts are numerous but individually small.

Retail/point-of-sale trade portal that publishes interviews with sector figures (e.g. SBK director Roman Kotlán) and vendor/partnership news at the merchant end of the acceptance chain — weak-signal colour that rarely appears in banking press.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank – Procurement principles page (RBI network, UA instance)
why_relevant: Raiffeisenbank CZ publishes no procurement-process page, but a sister RBI subsidiary does — 'transparency and partnership, principles of procurement activity'. As a proxy it shows the RBI house template for how a network bank runs supplier selection and e-auctions, letting an analyst infer the RB CZ process shape and the right questions to ask. Explicitly a proxy, not evidence about CZ.

Largest Czech commercial investigative desk; breaks stories on rigged/contested public IT contracts and the people behind supplier firms. An author page gives a clean, stable feed of the team's output.

Logistics trade title; relevant to payments through last-mile and parcel-locker technology with integrated payment terminals (COD, card acceptance at boxes). Low tender density but useful for supplier names in self-service payment hardware.

source_name: UniCredit Services (group ICT/Operations/Real Estate/Security/Procurement shared services)
why_relevant: UniCredit Services is the group entity providing ICT, Operations, Real Estate, Security AND Procurement services across the group — the mechanism by which UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia vendor selection is centralised in Milan/Vienna. Important caveat to record: UniCredit Services S.C.p.A. was merged into UniCredit S.p.A. on 1 October 2022, so the microsite may be legacy and current sourcing sits inside UniCredit S.p.A. — treat the page as a historical/structural pointer and verify current placement.

Public broadcaster's economics desk reports award outcomes with values and winning suppliers (e.g. the building-authority IS contract at CZK 24m won by Servodata). Free, archived and citable — good corroboration layer for paywalled reporting.
